147	/// Render the `budget:` block, with no trailing newline. When `show_rollup` is set and there are sections, the
148	/// `sections[n]{name,returned,total,truncated}:` table follows. An unknown `total` is the TOON `null` cell, because a
149	/// table row needs a value in every column.
150	pub(crate) fn render_budget_block(b: &BudgetSummary, show_rollup: bool) -> String {

# The Wisp / monokl Response Envelope

> **Status: Accepted ([ADR 10](../adr/0010-response-envelope-accepted.md)); partly implemented.** Sections, `BudgetSummary`, `ProvenanceBlock` and the JSON envelope (sections 1, 2, 3 and 5) are built in `michi-core`. Section 4 (the per-op index in `PartialSuccess`) lands in a separate PR. The published `outputSchema` in section 5 is not built. Where this text and the code differ, the code and [03-rust-api.md](03-rust-api.md) are current; the deviations are listed in [06-decisions.md](06-decisions.md) under "Envelope implementation deviations (gate 5)".

This design describes how one `AgentResponse` carries a monokl batch result or Wisp briefing: named sections, budget and provenance summaries, and index-bearing operation outcomes.

This is the michi half of a contract written down in three places. monokl's `docs/spec/08-library-session-api.md` §7 defines the batch `QueryResponse`; Wisp's `docs/02-architecture-and-contracts.md` §11–§12 defines the MCP surface that renders it; this doc defines what michi must hold for either of them to render through it. Nothing here changes how michi serializes MCP — that part is already right.

## The gap

Historical: this section describes `AgentResponse` before sections shipped. It held exactly one body. From `crates/michi-core/src/response.rs`:

| Field / type | Line | What it constrains |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `toon: ToonOptions` | 34 | One TOON slot: one `type_name` for the whole response, one `fields`/`rows` table |
| `single_item: Vec<KvItem>` | 36 | One KV slot |
| `toon.total_count: Option<usize>` | 34 | One count, for whichever slot renders |
| `enum RenderTarget { Unset, Toon, Kv }` (since removed) | 18–22 | The two slots were mutually exclusive |
| `toon.max_cell_len: usize` | 34 | Per-cell clamp, TOON path only, set by `truncate_cells_at()` (`DEFAULT_TRUNCATE_CELLS = 200`, line 25) |

Before this change, `items()` (line 59) set `target = RenderTarget::Toon`; `kv_items()` (line 108) set `Kv`; `body()` (line 194) dispatched on `target`, so `render()` read whichever setter ran last. Calling both silently dropped one. A ten-operation batch was not expressible: nine sections disappeared with no error and no signal that they existed. Sections fixed that, and the one-section-model change removed the slots, `RenderTarget`, `render_toon()` and `render_kv()` altogether: `items()` and `kv_items()` append sections now.

The truncation model has the same shape problem one level down. `truncate_cells_at` clamps a cell. `michi_core::truncate::Truncated { content, original_chars, removed }` describes a string. `michi_core::truncation::TruncationOutcome` describes one list, and `AgentResponse::truncation()` (now `truncated_section()`) turned it into the response's `totalCount` and one `help[]` line. None describes a response of several parts. The only envelope-level "there is more" signal is `total_count: Option<usize>` plus free-text hints — a bare integer with no per-section breakdown, no relation to a budget, and no way to say why anything was dropped. monokl's `BudgetReport` would have to be flattened into free-text `hint()` calls to reach the agent at all.

## What gets added

Five additions, in dependency order. All five are pure michi and always compiled — nothing here reaches outside the michi workspace for a type. The fourth changes an existing rendered format; the fifth extends `structured_content`.

### 1. Repeatable sections

```rust
/// One named block within a response. A response may hold any number.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
#[non_exhaustive]
pub struct Section {
    /// The section's type name — the identifier at the head of its TOON line, or the KV block's label.
    pub name: String,
    /// The section's contents.
    pub body: SectionBody,
    /// How many items this section actually carries.
    pub returned_count: usize,
    /// How many existed before truncation. `Some(n)` with `n > returned_count` is the "there is more" signal.
    pub total_count: Option<usize>,
    /// Whether producing this section dropped anything.
    pub truncated: bool,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
#[non_exhaustive]
pub enum SectionBody {
    /// A uniform list. Rendered through `michi_core::toon::ToonOptions`, per-cell truncation applied.
    Toon { fields: Vec<String>, rows: Vec<Vec<Value>> },
    /// A single receipt or a small set of labelled scalars.
    Kv(Vec<KvItem>),
    /// One string value, rendered as `name: <escaped value>`: escaped like any TOON string, never raw.
    Text(String),
}

impl Section {
    pub fn toon(name: impl Into<String>, fields: Vec<String>, rows: Vec<Vec<Value>>) -> Self;
    pub fn kv(name: impl Into<String>, items: Vec<KvItem>) -> Self;
    pub fn text(name: impl Into<String>, body: impl Into<String>) -> Self;
    /// Record the pre-truncation count. `total_count(Some(n))` with `n > returned_count` renders `totalCount: n`.
    pub fn total_count(self, total: Option<usize>) -> Self;
    pub fn truncated(self, truncated: bool) -> Self;
}

impl AgentResponse {
    /// Append a section. Sections render in insertion order — the caller owns ordering,
    /// because ordering is a policy the caller A/Bs (Wisp D-018), not something michi decides.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn section(self, s: Section) -> Self;
}
```

`items()` and `kv_items()` stay, as one-section sugar over the same storage: `items(rows, fields)` is `section(Section::toon(type_name, fields, rows))`, `kv_items(items)` is `section(Section::kv(type_name, items))`. `RenderTarget`, `render_toon()` and `render_kv()` are gone (see 06-decisions, "One section model").

**Sections are root keys.** A section renders as a root key of the TOON document (a list or text section under its name, a KV section as its item keys), so names must be distinct from each other and from the keys michi writes (`budget`, `sections`, `provenance`, `truncated`, `totalCount`, `help`, `recovery`; `error` and `message` when a section fails validation). The sugar names every section for the response, so it serves one list per response; several lists use `section(Section::toon(distinct_name, ..))`. A collision, or two equal provenance labels, never reaches the output as invalid TOON: the response renders the `toon_validation_failed` error naming the key, with `isError` true on every surface.

**Stability.** The envelope (`Section`, `BudgetSummary`, `ProvenanceBlock`) is unstable until a second independent consumer has used it (ADR 10). Its shape may change before 1.0, and the rustdoc on the three types says so.

Two invariants keep this compatible with what already ships:

- **A response with only `items()` or `kv_items()` renders as before, with the output changes listed in 06-decisions ("Output moves, all deliberate")**: `totalCount` only above the rows returned, and a `sections` array in the JSON. This replaces the original "byte-for-byte" rule, dropped when the one-section model removed the legacy slots (pre-1.0, ADR 9).
- **`returned_count` is derived, not trusted, for `Toon` and `Kv` bodies.** Render functions always succeed ([`PRINCIPLES.md`](../../PRINCIPLES.md)), so a `returned_count` disagreeing with `rows.len()` / `items.len()` is clamped to the real length with a `debug_assert!` alongside — the assert fires under `cargo nextest`, the clamp runs in release. `Text` bodies keep whatever the caller declared, since michi cannot count items in prose.

Rendered, a two-section response is just the sections in order:

```text
brief.symbols[12]{name,kind,file,line}:
  RetryPolicy,struct,src/retry/policy.rs,14
  …
totalCount: 40
brief.refs[5]{symbol,file,line}:
  RetryPolicy,src/http/client.rs,88
  …
```

### 2. A response-level budget report

```rust
/// What a budget block renders: the ceilings a caller was working under, what the response cost
/// against them, and what that cost each section. michi owns this type and names nothing from
/// Wisp or monokl.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
#[non_exhaustive]
pub struct BudgetSummary {
    /// Ceilings the caller set. Any of the three may be absent.
    pub max_tokens: Option<u64>,
    pub max_bytes: Option<u64>,
    pub max_items: Option<u64>,
    /// What the response cost, as the caller measured it.
    pub tokens_used: Option<u64>,
    pub bytes_used: Option<u64>,
    /// Whether the budget forced anything out of the response.
    pub truncated: bool,
    /// Per-section accounting, rendered in the order given.
    pub sections: Vec<SectionCost>,
}

/// One section's line in the budget roll-up.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
#[non_exhaustive]
pub struct SectionCost {
    pub name: String,
    pub returned: u64,
    /// How many existed before truncation, when the caller knows.
    pub total: Option<u64>,
    pub truncated: bool,
}

impl AgentResponse {
    /// Attach the response-level budget summary. One per response — a batch has one budget.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn budget(self, b: BudgetSummary) -> Self;
}
```

Every number is an `Option` or a plain counter, so a caller who measured only tokens fills two fields and leaves the rest empty. `u64` rather than `usize` because these values reach JSON, where a platform-dependent width means nothing.

Rendered once, after the last section, as a `budget:` KV block, with a roll-up naming each section's returned and total counts:

```text
budget:
  tokensUsed: 7412
  bytesUsed: 31208
  maxTokens: 8000
  maxBytes: 2097152
  truncated: true
sections[2]{name,returned,total,truncated}:
  brief.symbols,12,40,true
  brief.refs,5,5,false
```

Absent fields are omitted rather than rendered as `null`. The roll-up renders only when the response carries two or more sections. A single-section response already states its count in its own TOON header and `totalCount:` line, and repeating it costs tokens for nothing.

michi renders a budget; it never computes one. Which items survive a budget is the caller's decision — a BM25 cutoff, a reserved-floor allocator, monokl's `apply_budget` degrade-then-drop ladder. Reporting what got cut in a consistent agent-readable shape is the part every caller needs identically, which is exactly the split [`PRINCIPLES.md`](../../PRINCIPLES.md) describes for truncation.

### 3. A provenance slot

```rust
/// What a provenance block renders: a short ordered list of labelled values, plus the one string
/// a freshness check compares. michi assigns no meaning to any of them.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
#[non_exhaustive]
pub struct ProvenanceBlock {
    /// Rendered in order, one `label: value` line each.
    pub entries: Vec<ProvenanceEntry>,
    /// Rendered last when present.
    pub fingerprint: Option<String>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
#[non_exhaustive]
pub struct ProvenanceEntry {
    pub label: String,
    pub value: String,
}

impl AgentResponse {
    /// Attach the provenance block this response was computed against.
    /// One per response: a batch runs against one snapshot, so it has one provenance.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn provenance(self, p: ProvenanceBlock) -> Self;
}
```

A named pair rather than a `(String, String)` tuple: a tuple serializes as a two-element array, and a third-party reader of `structuredContent` then has nothing to key on.

Rendered as a KV block after `budget:`:

```text
provenance:
  analyzer: rust-analyzer@0.3.2
  observedAt: "1756950000000"
  precision: exact
  fingerprint: b3f1c0d2e4a58691
```

One block per response, not one per row — monokl's batch executes against a single `Snapshot`, so one fingerprint covers all N results rather than N fingerprints. Wisp's freshness tool (`wisp_check`) compares exactly the string in `fingerprint`.

The caller picks the labels. `monokl-agent` fills them from the `wisp_contracts::Provenance` its snapshot carries, `wisp-output` from the same type on Wisp's side, and a tool with no analyzer at all fills two entries and no fingerprint. michi renders what it was handed and validates none of it.

Per-edge precision stays out of the envelope. monokl carries `CapabilityPrecision` on each `DependencyEdge` and each `OpBudget` because a batch spanning an `Exact` TypeScript `refs` and a `Structural` Rust `dependents` has no honest single precision. michi renders whatever precision the caller wrote into a row or a provenance entry; it does not reduce several of them to one response-level value, and it has no type that could hold such a value.

### 4. Per-op outcomes: `PartialSuccess`, widened

`idempotency::PartialSuccess` already has the completed/failed/skipped trichotomy a batch needs. What it lacks is position: `Vec<String>` cannot express `results[i]` ↔ `ops[i]`, which is the ordering contract the batch API is built on (DataLoader's rule, restated in monokl §7.4 as an invariant). Reuse the type, widen the identifiers:

```rust
/// One operation's identity within a batch.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[non_exhaustive]
pub struct OpRef {
    /// Position in the caller's op slice. `results[index]` answers `ops[index]`.
    pub index: usize,
    /// Display name for the operation.
    pub operation: String,
    /// A stable machine token — `budget_exhausted`, `deadline`, `not_indexed` — never prose.
    /// michi does not define the vocabulary; the caller does.
    pub reason: Option<String>,
}

pub struct PartialSuccess {
    pub completed: Vec<OpRef>,   // was Vec<String>
    pub failed: Vec<FailedOp>,
    pub skipped: Vec<OpRef>,     // was Vec<String>
}

pub struct FailedOp {
    /// Position in the caller's op slice.
    pub index: usize,            // new
    pub operation: String,
    pub reason: String,
    pub recovery: Option<RecoveryHint>,
}
```

The index becomes a rendered column, so the correspondence survives into what the agent reads:

```text
partial_success: "2 completed, 1 failed, 1 skipped"
completed[2]{index,operation}:
  0,symbols
  1,dependents
failed[1]{index,operation,reason}:
  2,refs,"symbol not found: RetryPolicy"
skipped[1]{index,operation,reason}:
  3,search,budget_exhausted
```

**This one is a major bump.** Today's `completed[2]: a,b` inline array becomes `completed[2]{index,operation}:`, so existing rendered output differs — the SemVer table calls that major, and the exact-output tests in `idempotency.rs` (AC-032, AC-033) and the `snapshot_partial_success_full` insta snapshot change with it. There is no external consumer to break yet, which is the cheapest moment this change will ever have.

`exit_code()` is unchanged: `0` when nothing failed, `1` when anything did.

### 5. `structured_content` and a published `outputSchema`

`to_call_tool_result()` already builds `structured_content` from `render(OutputFormat::Json)`. Extend that JSON to carry the envelope:

```json
{
  "body": "…",
  "sections": [
    {
      "name": "brief.symbols",
      "kind": "toon",
      "fields": ["name", "kind", "file", "line"],
      "rows": [["RetryPolicy", "struct", "src/retry/policy.rs", 14]],
      "returnedCount": 12,
      "totalCount": 40,
      "truncated": true
    }
  ],
  "budget": {
    "tokensUsed": 7412,
    "bytesUsed": 31208,
    "maxTokens": 8000,
    "truncated": true,
    "sections": []
  },
  "provenance": {
    "entries": [{ "label": "analyzer", "value": "rust-analyzer@0.3.2" }],
    "fingerprint": "b3f1c0d2e4a58691"
  },
  "hints": ["…"],
  "recovery": [],
  "isError": false
}
```

Every key in that object is camelCase — `returnedCount`, `totalCount`, `tokensUsed`, `maxTokens`, `isError`. The rendered examples above are the specification of that, not an illustration of it: a third-party harness plugin reading this JSON without linking any Rust is a first-class consumer, and `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]` on every envelope type is what keeps the spelling stable. Labels inside `provenance.entries` are caller-supplied strings and michi does not case-convert them.

`sections`, `budget`, and `provenance` appear only when set. A response with no body, budget or provenance still emits exactly `body`, `hints`, `recovery`, `isError` — the four keys AC-004 pins. `items()` and `kv_items()` add a section, so a response built with them also carries `sections`; AC-004 asserts "the four, plus the envelope keys that were set".

The schema is published through the existing `schemars` feature: `Section`, `SectionBody`, `BudgetSummary`, `SectionCost`, `ProvenanceBlock`, and `ProvenanceEntry` derive `JsonSchema`, and the server declares the result as its tool's `outputSchema`. MCP makes conformance binding once a schema is declared — servers MUST return conforming structured results, clients SHOULD validate — which is the reason to publish one rather than leave the shape implicit. The token-budget caveat in [06-decisions.md](06-decisions.md) still applies: `outputSchema` enters the context window at `tools/list` time, so declare it on always-loaded tools, not on deferred ones.

## The render path

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    S1["Section — Toon"]
    S2["Section — Kv"]
    SN["Section — Text"]
    B["BudgetSummary"]
    P["ProvenanceBlock"]
    HR["hints / recovery"]

    S1 --> AR
    S2 --> AR
    SN --> AR
    B --> AR
    P --> AR
    HR --> AR

    AR["AgentResponse — N sections"]

    AR -->|"render_text()"| text["sections in order, then budget:, provenance:, help[], recovery[]"]
    AR -->|"render(OutputFormat::Json)"| json["sections[], budget, provenance, hints, recovery, isError"]

    text --> block["ContentBlock { audience: [assistant] }"]
    human["human_content()"] --> ublock["ContentBlock { audience: [user] }"]

    block --> ctr["mcp::CallToolResult"]
    ublock --> ctr
    json --> ctr
    ctr --> wire["MCP tools/call JSON"]
```

Everything below `AgentResponse` in that diagram already exists and is unchanged. `CallToolResult { content, is_error, structured_content }`, `ContentBlock.audience: Vec<Audience>` matching MCP's array-typed `annotations.audience`, the private `*Wire` structs that add the `"type": "text"` discriminator and nest `audience` under `annotations`, and `structured_content` parsed into embedded JSON rather than double-encoded — see [04-mcp-and-napi.md](04-mcp-and-napi.md). The gap is in what `AgentResponse` can hold, not in how it reaches the wire.

## Where these types come from

`Section`, `SectionBody`, `BudgetSummary`, `SectionCost`, `ProvenanceBlock`, and `ProvenanceEntry` are defined in `michi-core`. michi reaches outside its own workspace for none of them, and in particular it does not depend on `wisp-contracts`.

That is a change from an earlier draft of this document, which imported `wisp_contracts::BudgetReport` and `wisp_contracts::Provenance` behind an optional `contracts` feature. michi publishes to crates.io first, so a michi release cannot name a crate that is not published yet — and a feature gate does not fix an ordering problem, since an optional dependency still has to resolve. The vocabulary argument that justified the import is sound and unchanged: `Provenance` and `BudgetReport` are meanings Wisp and monokl must agree on, and they belong in a permissively licensed crate for the harness plugins that cannot link AGPL code. What michi needs is not that meaning. It is the handful of numbers and strings a block renders, which is a smaller thing, and michi's own.

The conversion lives in the consumer, which already links both sides:

| Consumer | Holds | Converts into |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `wisp-output` | `wisp_contracts::BudgetReport`, filled by `wisp-context`'s per-section allocator | `BudgetSummary` |
| `monokl-agent` | `wisp_contracts::BudgetReport`, filled by its own `apply_budget` | `BudgetSummary` |
| both of the above | `wisp_contracts::Provenance`, read off the snapshot the batch ran against | `ProvenanceBlock` |

Each conversion is a few dozen lines of field copying in a crate that imports contracts anyway. michi imports it in no build, and learns nothing about how a `Budget` is allocated, what a `WorkspaceFingerprint` hashes, or how `CapabilityPrecision` ranks.

`michi renders a budget; it never computes one` is what makes that split hold. Under monokl `08 §7.5` there are two independent producers of a budget report — `monokl-agent` for the CLI and Wisp's `wisp-context` for a briefing — and michi is the only renderer both share. A renderer needs the numbers, not the allocator that produced them, so the numbers are all the envelope takes.

**No new feature flag.** All six types are built from types michi already owns, so all six are always compiled and gate 2's small default dependency set is untouched — there is no dependency to gate. `render_json()` stays hand-built and `serde_json`-free: michi owns these shapes, so it emits their keys the way it emits every other key today, and the `budget` and `provenance` JSON keys appear in a default build. The `serde` and `schemars` derives ride the existing optional features and add nothing to the default.

## Rules this envelope has to hold

| Rule | Why |
| --- | --- |
| **Never fail closed on overflow.** Partial results, plus counts, plus a refinement hint. Never "no content is returned." | Serena's `find_symbol` returns nothing once `max_answer_chars` is exceeded, leaving the agent to guess a narrower query with no information about what it missed. Partial results plus `total_count` plus a hint naming the refinement operator is strictly more useful, and it is the behavior monokl already has. Wisp D-019 states the same rule for its MCP surface. |
| **No pagination cursors on tool results.** | MCP defines `cursor`/`nextCursor` only for list operations — `tools/list` paginates, `tools/call` results have no cursor field, and the 2026-07-28 release candidate does not add one. A cursor on a tool result is a private convention no client will honor. Truncation plus counts plus a hint is the signal that works. |
| **TOON for five or more uniform rows; KV for a single receipt.** | TOON's saving comes from stating field names once across many rows. Below roughly five rows the header costs more than the repetition it removes, and a one-item result reads better as `key: value` lines. `SectionBody` carries both so one response can mix them section by section. |
| **michi never reads its own TOON back.** | TOON is a rendering target. No render path parses it, and no consumer should: a caller that needs the data as data reads `structured_content`, which carries the same values already typed. Wisp states the same rule for itself. The round-trip parser exists to prove the renderer's output is grammar-valid in property tests, not as a data path. |
| **Sections render in insertion order.** | Ordering is a policy the caller measures (Wisp's Prism A/Bs it). michi renders what it was handed, in the order it was handed. |

## The Wisp arrangement

Wisp's `wisp-output` crate depends on michi through a **local path dependency during coordinated development**, and the publish order runs one way: michi publishes first, and Wisp is not published until michi has a versioned release compatible with Wisp's license and MSRV (Wisp D-006). michi's declared MSRV is `1.93`.

Nothing in Wisp gates a michi release, and no consumer integration gates it either (see [ADR 4](../adr/0004-publish-before-consumer-integration.md)). michi publishes first so Wisp can integrate against a versioned dependency, then Wisp can publish its own package. A tagged Git dependency (`michi-core = { git = "…", tag = "michi@0.x.y" }`) remains useful during coordinated development.

Licensing is settled, not open. michi is `FSL-1.1-MIT`, matching Wisp's upper layers and Lumen, and monokl carries the same license. With all three on `FSL-1.1-MIT`, the FSL-linking-AGPL redistribution conflict this section used to flag no longer exists.

## What this is not

**Not a Wisp type, and not a monokl type.** `Section`, `SectionBody`, `BudgetSummary`, and `ProvenanceBlock` name nothing from either domain, and michi's manifest names neither crate. Any orin-dx tool returning heterogeneous results in one call — a status command reporting several subsystems, a CLI answering a compound query — uses the same envelope, and a tool with one list still writes `items()` and never sees a `Section`.

**Not a batch executor.** michi has no async runtime and no scheduler. Dedupe, deadlines, snapshot atomicity, and the budget allocation policy are monokl's `query()`; michi receives the outcome and renders it.

**Not a budget allocator.** `BudgetSummary` is a record of a decision already made. Which items survive is the caller's algorithm, and michi has no opinion about it.

**Not the whole of what monokl asks michi for.** `MICHI-ADJUSTMENTS.md` under monokl's `.claude/plans/` carried a separate set of asks that this document does not cover, and they have since shipped on their own: the five bug fixes (`escape_value` now escapes line breaks instead of dropping them, `toon::list()` headers are the union of every item's fields, the `debug_assert!` arity panic is gone, `AgentResponse` renders a `validate()` failure as a `toon_validation_failed` error body, and `DomainError::render()` escapes newlines in its message and hints), `TruncationOutcome<T>` with `truncate_by_count` and `truncate_by_size` (in place of the sketched `truncate_by_bytes`; see [03 — `truncation`](03-rust-api.md#truncation--what-a-list-cap-cut)), and `DomainError::from_error()` (the `from_error_chain()` ask), which keeps the `source()` chain as `causes`. It explicitly did not propose new `ErrorCode` variants. None of it contradicts this envelope — it was orthogonal work on escaping, truncation, and error rendering.

**Not fully clear of michi's third gate yet, and the honest reading matters.** The gate asks for independent real tools that would otherwise hand-roll the identical pattern, and warns that one tool using a pattern heavily is one data point rather than proof. monokl's batch response and Wisp's briefing are two consumers, but Wisp consumes monokl, so they are not independent in the sense the gate means. What carries the case is the survey behind it: across Sourcegraph, Serena, MCP itself, and LSP, nobody attaches a single top-level budget report across multiple result sections — the pattern is absent from the prior art rather than reinvented in it. That is an argument from a gap, which is weaker than the four-for-four evidence `help[]` hints cleared the gate with. Whether that argument carries the gate on its own, whether a third michi consumer has to show up first, or whether the gate is waived for this envelope, is michi's call and nobody else's — Wisp does not clear michi's gates, and michi does not wait on Wisp to attempt it.

| `enum RenderTarget { Unset, Toon, Kv }` (since removed) | 18–22 | The two slots were mutually exclusive |
| `toon.max_cell_len: usize` | 34 | Per-cell clamp, TOON path only, set by `truncate_cells_at()` (`DEFAULT_TRUNCATE_CELLS = 200`, line 25) |

Before this change, `items()` (line 59) set `target = RenderTarget::Toon`; `kv_items()` (line 108) set `Kv`; `body()` (line 194) dispatched on `target`, so `render()` read whichever setter ran last. Calling both silently dropped one. A ten-operation batch was not expressible: nine sections disappeared with no error and no signal that they existed. Sections fixed that, and the one-section-model change removed the slots, `RenderTarget`, `render_toon()` and `render_kv()` altogether: `items()` and `kv_items()` append sections now.

The truncation model has the same shape problem one level down. `truncate_cells_at` clamps a cell. `michi_core::truncate::Truncated { content, original_chars, removed }` describes a string. `michi_core::truncation::TruncationOutcome` describes one list, and `AgentResponse::truncation()` (now `truncated_section()`) turned it into the response's `totalCount` and one `help[]` line. None describes a response of several parts. The only envelope-level "there is more" signal is `total_count: Option<usize>` plus free-text hints — a bare integer with no per-section breakdown, no relation to a budget, and no way to say why anything was dropped. monokl's `BudgetReport` would have to be flattened into free-text `hint()` calls to reach the agent at all.

## What gets added

Five additions, in dependency order. All five are pure michi and always compiled — nothing here reaches outside the michi workspace for a type. The fourth changes an existing rendered format; the fifth extends `structured_content`.

### 1. Repeatable sections

```rust
/// One named block within a response. A response may hold any number.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
#[non_exhaustive]
pub struct Section {
    /// The section's type name — the identifier at the head of its TOON line, or the KV block's label.
    pub name: String,
    /// The section's contents.
    pub body: SectionBody,
    /// How many items this section actually carries.
    pub returned_count: usize,
    /// How many existed before truncation. `Some(n)` with `n > returned_count` is the "there is more" signal.
    pub total_count: Option<usize>,
    /// Whether producing this section dropped anything.
    pub truncated: bool,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
#[non_exhaustive]
pub enum SectionBody {
    /// A uniform list. Rendered through `michi_core::toon::ToonOptions`, per-cell truncation applied.
    Toon { fields: Vec<String>, rows: Vec<Vec<Value>> },
    /// A single receipt or a small set of labelled scalars.
    Kv(Vec<KvItem>),
    /// One string value, rendered as `name: <escaped value>`: escaped like any TOON string, never raw.
    Text(String),
}

impl Section {
    pub fn toon(name: impl Into<String>, fields: Vec<String>, rows: Vec<Vec<Value>>) -> Self;
    pub fn kv(name: impl Into<String>, items: Vec<KvItem>) -> Self;
    pub fn text(name: impl Into<String>, body: impl Into<String>) -> Self;
    /// Record the pre-truncation count. `total_count(Some(n))` with `n > returned_count` renders `totalCount: n`.
    pub fn total_count(self, total: Option<usize>) -> Self;
    pub fn truncated(self, truncated: bool) -> Self;
}

impl AgentResponse {
    /// Append a section. Sections render in insertion order — the caller owns ordering,
    /// because ordering is a policy the caller A/Bs (Wisp D-018), not something michi decides.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn section(self, s: Section) -> Self;
}
```

`items()` and `kv_items()` stay, as one-section sugar over the same storage: `items(rows, fields)` is `section(Section::toon(type_name, fields, rows))`, `kv_items(items)` is `section(Section::kv(type_name, items))`. `RenderTarget`, `render_toon()` and `render_kv()` are gone (see 06-decisions, "One section model").

**Sections are root keys.** A section renders as a root key of the TOON document (a list or text section under its name, a KV section as its item keys), so names must be distinct from each other and from the keys michi writes (`budget`, `sections`, `provenance`, `truncated`, `totalCount`, `help`, `recovery`; `error` and `message` when a section fails validation). The sugar names every section for the response, so it serves one list per response; several lists use `section(Section::toon(distinct_name, ..))`. A collision, or two equal provenance labels, never reaches the output as invalid TOON: the response renders the `toon_validation_failed` error naming the key, with `isError` true on every surface.

**Stability.** The envelope (`Section`, `BudgetSummary`, `ProvenanceBlock`) is unstable until a second independent consumer has used it (ADR 10). Its shape may change before 1.0, and the rustdoc on the three types says so.

Two invariants keep this compatible with what already ships:

- **A response with only `items()` or `kv_items()` renders as before, with the output changes listed in 06-decisions ("Output moves, all deliberate")**: `totalCount` only above the rows returned, and a `sections` array in the JSON. This replaces the original "byte-for-byte" rule, dropped when the one-section model removed the legacy slots (pre-1.0, ADR 9).
- **`returned_count` is derived, not trusted, for `Toon` and `Kv` bodies.** Render functions always succeed ([`PRINCIPLES.md`](../../PRINCIPLES.md)), so a `returned_count` disagreeing with `rows.len()` / `items.len()` is clamped to the real length with a `debug_assert!` alongside — the assert fires under `cargo nextest`, the clamp runs in release. `Text` bodies keep whatever the caller declared, since michi cannot count items in prose.

Rendered, a two-section response is just the sections in order:

```text
brief.symbols[12]{name,kind,file,line}:
  RetryPolicy,struct,src/retry/policy.rs,14
  …
totalCount: 40
brief.refs[5]{symbol,file,line}:
  RetryPolicy,src/http/client.rs,88
  …
```

### 2. A response-level budget report

```rust
/// What a budget block renders: the ceilings a caller was working under, what the response cost
/// against them, and what that cost each section. michi owns this type and names nothing from
/// Wisp or monokl.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
#[non_exhaustive]
pub struct BudgetSummary {
    /// Ceilings the caller set. Any of the three may be absent.
    pub max_tokens: Option<u64>,
    pub max_bytes: Option<u64>,
    pub max_items: Option<u64>,
    /// What the response cost, as the caller measured it.
    pub tokens_used: Option<u64>,
    pub bytes_used: Option<u64>,
    /// Whether the budget forced anything out of the response.
    pub truncated: bool,
    /// Per-section accounting, rendered in the order given.
    pub sections: Vec<SectionCost>,
}

/// One section's line in the budget roll-up.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
#[non_exhaustive]
pub struct SectionCost {
    pub name: String,
    pub returned: u64,
    /// How many existed before truncation, when the caller knows.
    pub total: Option<u64>,
    pub truncated: bool,
}

impl AgentResponse {
    /// Attach the response-level budget summary. One per response — a batch has one budget.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn budget(self, b: BudgetSummary) -> Self;
}
```

Every number is an `Option` or a plain counter, so a caller who measured only tokens fills two fields and leaves the rest empty. `u64` rather than `usize` because these values reach JSON, where a platform-dependent width means nothing.

Rendered once, after the last section, as a `budget:` KV block, with a roll-up naming each section's returned and total counts:

```text
budget:
  tokensUsed: 7412
  bytesUsed: 31208
  maxTokens: 8000
  maxBytes: 2097152
  truncated: true
sections[2]{name,returned,total,truncated}:
  brief.symbols,12,40,true
  brief.refs,5,5,false
```

Absent fields are omitted rather than rendered as `null`. The roll-up renders only when the response carries two or more sections. A single-section response already states its count in its own TOON header and `totalCount:` line, and repeating it costs tokens for nothing.

michi renders a budget; it never computes one. Which items survive a budget is the caller's decision — a BM25 cutoff, a reserved-floor allocator, monokl's `apply_budget` degrade-then-drop ladder. Reporting what got cut in a consistent agent-readable shape is the part every caller needs identically, which is exactly the split [`PRINCIPLES.md`](../../PRINCIPLES.md) describes for truncation.

### 3. A provenance slot

```rust
/// What a provenance block renders: a short ordered list of labelled values, plus the one string
/// a freshness check compares. michi assigns no meaning to any of them.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
#[non_exhaustive]
pub struct ProvenanceBlock {
    /// Rendered in order, one `label: value` line each.
    pub entries: Vec<ProvenanceEntry>,
    /// Rendered last when present.
    pub fingerprint: Option<String>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
#[non_exhaustive]
pub struct ProvenanceEntry {
    pub label: String,
    pub value: String,
}

impl AgentResponse {
    /// Attach the provenance block this response was computed against.
    /// One per response: a batch runs against one snapshot, so it has one provenance.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn provenance(self, p: ProvenanceBlock) -> Self;
}
```

A named pair rather than a `(String, String)` tuple: a tuple serializes as a two-element array, and a third-party reader of `structuredContent` then has nothing to key on.

Rendered as a KV block after `budget:`:

```text
provenance:
  analyzer: rust-analyzer@0.3.2
  observedAt: "1756950000000"
  precision: exact
  fingerprint: b3f1c0d2e4a58691
```

One block per response, not one per row — monokl's batch executes against a single `Snapshot`, so one fingerprint covers all N results rather than N fingerprints. Wisp's freshness tool (`wisp_check`) compares exactly the string in `fingerprint`.

The caller picks the labels. `monokl-agent` fills them from the `wisp_contracts::Provenance` its snapshot carries, `wisp-output` from the same type on Wisp's side, and a tool with no analyzer at all fills two entries and no fingerprint. michi renders what it was handed and validates none of it.

Per-edge precision stays out of the envelope. monokl carries `CapabilityPrecision` on each `DependencyEdge` and each `OpBudget` because a batch spanning an `Exact` TypeScript `refs` and a `Structural` Rust `dependents` has no honest single precision. michi renders whatever precision the caller wrote into a row or a provenance entry; it does not reduce several of them to one response-level value, and it has no type that could hold such a value.

### 4. Per-op outcomes: `PartialSuccess`, widened

`idempotency::PartialSuccess` already has the completed/failed/skipped trichotomy a batch needs. What it lacks is position: `Vec<String>` cannot express `results[i]` ↔ `ops[i]`, which is the ordering contract the batch API is built on (DataLoader's rule, restated in monokl §7.4 as an invariant). Reuse the type, widen the identifiers:

```rust
/// One operation's identity within a batch.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[non_exhaustive]
pub struct OpRef {
    /// Position in the caller's op slice. `results[index]` answers `ops[index]`.
    pub index: usize,
    /// Display name for the operation.
    pub operation: String,
    /// A stable machine token — `budget_exhausted`, `deadline`, `not_indexed` — never prose.
    /// michi does not define the vocabulary; the caller does.
    pub reason: Option<String>,
}

pub struct PartialSuccess {
    pub completed: Vec<OpRef>,   // was Vec<String>
    pub failed: Vec<FailedOp>,
    pub skipped: Vec<OpRef>,     // was Vec<String>
}

pub struct FailedOp {
    /// Position in the caller's op slice.
    pub index: usize,            // new
    pub operation: String,
    pub reason: String,
    pub recovery: Option<RecoveryHint>,
}
```

The index becomes a rendered column, so the correspondence survives into what the agent reads:

```text
partial_success: "2 completed, 1 failed, 1 skipped"
completed[2]{index,operation}:
  0,symbols
  1,dependents
failed[1]{index,operation,reason}:
  2,refs,"symbol not found: RetryPolicy"
skipped[1]{index,operation,reason}:
  3,search,budget_exhausted
```

**This one is a major bump.** Today's `completed[2]: a,b` inline array becomes `completed[2]{index,operation}:`, so existing rendered output differs — the SemVer table calls that major, and the exact-output tests in `idempotency.rs` (AC-032, AC-033) and the `snapshot_partial_success_full` insta snapshot change with it. There is no external consumer to break yet, which is the cheapest moment this change will ever have.

`exit_code()` is unchanged: `0` when nothing failed, `1` when anything did.

### 5. `structured_content` and a published `outputSchema`

`to_call_tool_result()` already builds `structured_content` from `render(OutputFormat::Json)`. Extend that JSON to carry the envelope:

```json
{
  "body": "…",
  "sections": [
    {
      "name": "brief.symbols",
      "kind": "toon",
      "fields": ["name", "kind", "file", "line"],
      "rows": [["RetryPolicy", "struct", "src/retry/policy.rs", 14]],
      "returnedCount": 12,
      "totalCount": 40,
      "truncated": true
    }
  ],
  "budget": {
    "tokensUsed": 7412,
    "bytesUsed": 31208,
    "maxTokens": 8000,
    "truncated": true,
    "sections": []
  },
  "provenance": {
    "entries": [{ "label": "analyzer", "value": "rust-analyzer@0.3.2" }],
    "fingerprint": "b3f1c0d2e4a58691"
  },
  "hints": ["…"],
  "recovery": [],
  "isError": false
}
```

Every key in that object is camelCase — `returnedCount`, `totalCount`, `tokensUsed`, `maxTokens`, `isError`. The rendered examples above are the specification of that, not an illustration of it: a third-party harness plugin reading this JSON without linking any Rust is a first-class consumer, and `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]` on every envelope type is what keeps the spelling stable. Labels inside `provenance.entries` are caller-supplied strings and michi does not case-convert them.

`sections`, `budget`, and `provenance` appear only when set. A response with no body, budget or provenance still emits exactly `body`, `hints`, `recovery`, `isError` — the four keys AC-004 pins. `items()` and `kv_items()` add a section, so a response built with them also carries `sections`; AC-004 asserts "the four, plus the envelope keys that were set".

The schema is published through the existing `schemars` feature: `Section`, `SectionBody`, `BudgetSummary`, `SectionCost`, `ProvenanceBlock`, and `ProvenanceEntry` derive `JsonSchema`, and the server declares the result as its tool's `outputSchema`. MCP makes conformance binding once a schema is declared — servers MUST return conforming structured results, clients SHOULD validate — which is the reason to publish one rather than leave the shape implicit. The token-budget caveat in [06-decisions.md](06-decisions.md) still applies: `outputSchema` enters the context window at `tools/list` time, so declare it on always-loaded tools, not on deferred ones.

## The render path

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    S1["Section — Toon"]
    S2["Section — Kv"]
    SN["Section — Text"]
    B["BudgetSummary"]
    P["ProvenanceBlock"]
    HR["hints / recovery"]

    S1 --> AR
    S2 --> AR
    SN --> AR
    B --> AR
    P --> AR
    HR --> AR

    AR["AgentResponse — N sections"]

    AR -->|"render_text()"| text["sections in order, then budget:, provenance:, help[], recovery[]"]
    AR -->|"render(OutputFormat::Json)"| json["sections[], budget, provenance, hints, recovery, isError"]

    text --> block["ContentBlock { audience: [assistant] }"]
    human["human_content()"] --> ublock["ContentBlock { audience: [user] }"]

    block --> ctr["mcp::CallToolResult"]
    ublock --> ctr
    json --> ctr
    ctr --> wire["MCP tools/call JSON"]
```

Everything below `AgentResponse` in that diagram already exists and is unchanged. `CallToolResult { content, is_error, structured_content }`, `ContentBlock.audience: Vec<Audience>` matching MCP's array-typed `annotations.audience`, the private `*Wire` structs that add the `"type": "text"` discriminator and nest `audience` under `annotations`, and `structured_content` parsed into embedded JSON rather than double-encoded — see [04-mcp-and-napi.md](04-mcp-and-napi.md). The gap is in what `AgentResponse` can hold, not in how it reaches the wire.

## Where these types come from

`Section`, `SectionBody`, `BudgetSummary`, `SectionCost`, `ProvenanceBlock`, and `ProvenanceEntry` are defined in `michi-core`. michi reaches outside its own workspace for none of them, and in particular it does not depend on `wisp-contracts`.

That is a change from an earlier draft of this document, which imported `wisp_contracts::BudgetReport` and `wisp_contracts::Provenance` behind an optional `contracts` feature. michi publishes to crates.io first, so a michi release cannot name a crate that is not published yet — and a feature gate does not fix an ordering problem, since an optional dependency still has to resolve. The vocabulary argument that justified the import is sound and unchanged: `Provenance` and `BudgetReport` are meanings Wisp and monokl must agree on, and they belong in a permissively licensed crate for the harness plugins that cannot link AGPL code. What michi needs is not that meaning. It is the handful of numbers and strings a block renders, which is a smaller thing, and michi's own.

The conversion lives in the consumer, which already links both sides:

| Consumer | Holds | Converts into |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `wisp-output` | `wisp_contracts::BudgetReport`, filled by `wisp-context`'s per-section allocator | `BudgetSummary` |
| `monokl-agent` | `wisp_contracts::BudgetReport`, filled by its own `apply_budget` | `BudgetSummary` |
| both of the above | `wisp_contracts::Provenance`, read off the snapshot the batch ran against | `ProvenanceBlock` |

Each conversion is a few dozen lines of field copying in a crate that imports contracts anyway. michi imports it in no build, and learns nothing about how a `Budget` is allocated, what a `WorkspaceFingerprint` hashes, or how `CapabilityPrecision` ranks.

`michi renders a budget; it never computes one` is what makes that split hold. Under monokl `08 §7.5` there are two independent producers of a budget report — `monokl-agent` for the CLI and Wisp's `wisp-context` for a briefing — and michi is the only renderer both share. A renderer needs the numbers, not the allocator that produced them, so the numbers are all the envelope takes.

**No new feature flag.** All six types are built from types michi already owns, so all six are always compiled and gate 2's small default dependency set is untouched — there is no dependency to gate. `render_json()` stays hand-built and `serde_json`-free: michi owns these shapes, so it emits their keys the way it emits every other key today, and the `budget` and `provenance` JSON keys appear in a default build. The `serde` and `schemars` derives ride the existing optional features and add nothing to the default.

## Rules this envelope has to hold

| Rule | Why |
| --- | --- |
| **Never fail closed on overflow.** Partial results, plus counts, plus a refinement hint. Never "no content is returned." | Serena's `find_symbol` returns nothing once `max_answer_chars` is exceeded, leaving the agent to guess a narrower query with no information about what it missed. Partial results plus `total_count` plus a hint naming the refinement operator is strictly more useful, and it is the behavior monokl already has. Wisp D-019 states the same rule for its MCP surface. |
| **No pagination cursors on tool results.** | MCP defines `cursor`/`nextCursor` only for list operations — `tools/list` paginates, `tools/call` results have no cursor field, and the 2026-07-28 release candidate does not add one. A cursor on a tool result is a private convention no client will honor. Truncation plus counts plus a hint is the signal that works. |
| **TOON for five or more uniform rows; KV for a single receipt.** | TOON's saving comes from stating field names once across many rows. Below roughly five rows the header costs more than the repetition it removes, and a one-item result reads better as `key: value` lines. `SectionBody` carries both so one response can mix them section by section. |
| **michi never reads its own TOON back.** | TOON is a rendering target. No render path parses it, and no consumer should: a caller that needs the data as data reads `structured_content`, which carries the same values already typed. Wisp states the same rule for itself. The round-trip parser exists to prove the renderer's output is grammar-valid in property tests, not as a data path. |
| **Sections render in insertion order.** | Ordering is a policy the caller measures (Wisp's Prism A/Bs it). michi renders what it was handed, in the order it was handed. |

## The Wisp arrangement

Wisp's `wisp-output` crate depends on michi through a **local path dependency during coordinated development**, and the publish order runs one way: michi publishes first, and Wisp is not published until michi has a versioned release compatible with Wisp's license and MSRV (Wisp D-006). michi's declared MSRV is `1.93`.

Nothing in Wisp gates a michi release, and no consumer integration gates it either (see [ADR 4](../adr/0004-publish-before-consumer-integration.md)). michi publishes first so Wisp can integrate against a versioned dependency, then Wisp can publish its own package. A tagged Git dependency (`michi-core = { git = "…", tag = "michi@0.x.y" }`) remains useful during coordinated development.

Licensing is settled, not open. michi is `FSL-1.1-MIT`, matching Wisp's upper layers and Lumen, and monokl carries the same license. With all three on `FSL-1.1-MIT`, the FSL-linking-AGPL redistribution conflict this section used to flag no longer exists.

## What this is not

**Not a Wisp type, and not a monokl type.** `Section`, `SectionBody`, `BudgetSummary`, and `ProvenanceBlock` name nothing from either domain, and michi's manifest names neither crate. Any orin-dx tool returning heterogeneous results in one call — a status command reporting several subsystems, a CLI answering a compound query — uses the same envelope, and a tool with one list still writes `items()` and never sees a `Section`.

**Not a batch executor.** michi has no async runtime and no scheduler. Dedupe, deadlines, snapshot atomicity, and the budget allocation policy are monokl's `query()`; michi receives the outcome and renders it.

**Not a budget allocator.** `BudgetSummary` is a record of a decision already made. Which items survive is the caller's algorithm, and michi has no opinion about it.

**Not the whole of what monokl asks michi for.** `MICHI-ADJUSTMENTS.md` under monokl's `.claude/plans/` carried a separate set of asks that this document does not cover, and they have since shipped on their own: the five bug fixes (`escape_value` now escapes line breaks instead of dropping them, `toon::list()` headers are the union of every item's fields, the `debug_assert!` arity panic is gone, `AgentResponse` renders a `validate()` failure as a `toon_validation_failed` error body, and `DomainError::render()` escapes newlines in its message and hints), `TruncationOutcome<T>` with `truncate_by_count` and `truncate_by_size` (in place of the sketched `truncate_by_bytes`; see [03 — `truncation`](03-rust-api.md#truncation--what-a-list-cap-cut)), and `DomainError::from_error()` (the `from_error_chain()` ask), which keeps the `source()` chain as `causes`. It explicitly did not propose new `ErrorCode` variants. None of it contradicts this envelope — it was orthogonal work on escaping, truncation, and error rendering.

**Not fully clear of michi's third gate yet, and the honest reading matters.** The gate asks for independent real tools that would otherwise hand-roll the identical pattern, and warns that one tool using a pattern heavily is one data point rather than proof. monokl's batch response and Wisp's briefing are two consumers, but Wisp consumes monokl, so they are not independent in the sense the gate means. What carries the case is the survey behind it: across Sourcegraph, Serena, MCP itself, and LSP, nobody attaches a single top-level budget report across multiple result sections — the pattern is absent from the prior art rather than reinvented in it. That is an argument from a gap, which is weaker than the four-for-four evidence `help[]` hints cleared the gate with. Whether that argument carries the gate on its own, whether a third michi consumer has to show up first, or whether the gate is waived for this envelope, is michi's call and nobody else's — Wisp does not clear michi's gates, and michi does not wait on Wisp to attempt it.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Compares `monokl search` with ripgrep on pinned public repositories.

monokl is meant to return the few right answers, not everything that matches. So ripgrep supplies the ground truth for
what is right, and the score rewards targeting:

- definitions: files that declare the identifier. The gate is whether one of them is among monokl's first `--top` files
  (hit@top), because an agent that asks for a symbol must be shown where it is declared, early.
- declaration_in_output: whether the declaration's own line appears in monokl's output, so the agent needs no second
  read of the file. Reported, not gated.
- cost: files and output size monokl returns with its default caps, against one `rg -n` call. rg wins on a bare
  identifier, so this is the floor to beat; monokl's case is the question that takes rg several calls.
- test files are left out of the lists, as monokl leaves them out by default. `--tests` also runs monokl with its test
  flag and reports how many test files with the word it returned, ungated.

Questions (scripts/rg-compare.questions) score the case monokl exists for: two to four words that take several rg calls,
with a known answer file and symbol. Each reports the answer file's rank, whether the declaration line is in the output,
the rg route's narrowing cost (files with any word, files with all words, bytes of one `rg -n` call for any word) and
monokl's output bytes. The gate is the answer file in monokl's first `--top` files for at least `--min-question-recall`
of the questions.

Member questions use the same file format with the symbol cell written `member:name`: the answer is a method,
constructor, accessor or arrow-function property declared on an indented line inside a class. The script re-checks that
line with rg and scores them on their own line, apart from the top-level questions. A member question is a hit when the
answer file is in monokl's first `--top` files and the member's declaration line is in the output; the gate is
`--min-member-recall`.

Each repository has a language (the optional fourth column of rg-compare.repos, default `ts`). A `rust` repository is
searched with `*.rs`, its declarations are `fn|struct|enum|trait|type|const|static|mod|macro_rules!` at the start of a
line (optional `pub`, `pub(crate)`), and its members are `fn` and `const` on an indented line inside an `impl` or
`trait` block. `tests/` directories are test files; `#[cfg(test)]` modules are test code for the analyzer, but this
script works on whole files and cannot split them, so a `mod tests` is skipped when sampling and test code inside
source files still counts as source here. monokl runs without `--language`, which searches every registered language,
so no flag is passed. Rust rows (identifiers, questions and members together) are scored apart from the TypeScript
gates and gated by `--min-rust-recall`, which defaults to 0.9 now that the analyzer ships. A Rust repository that monokl
cannot search yet scores 0 hits, which the report states.

Held-out rows guard against tuning to the pinned set. A repository whose options include `held-out` in rg-compare.repos is
never sampled for identifiers, and its questions carry a fifth cell `held_out` in rg-compare.questions. They are scored
like the tuned questions and members but on their own `held-out questions` and `held-out members` lines, gated by
`--min-heldout-recall` and `--min-heldout-member-recall`, both 0.9, set from the first measured scores (23/24 and 12/12). Ranking changes may be tuned
on the other rows and must be reported on these.

A repository whose options also include `report-only` is scored and printed per repository but never gates; the marker
comes off once the repository passes 0.9. Gated held-out Rust rows are pooled on a `held-out rust` line, gated by
`--min-heldout-rust-recall`.

Wall time is reported. Repositories are cloned on demand into target/rg-compare.
"""

import argparse
import json
import re
import statistics
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""What a coding agent pays to answer each rg-compare question with `monokl search` against ripgrep alone. No model, no
timing: bytes, estimated tokens and turns, all deterministic for a pinned checkout and a binary.

Rows are the rg-compare harness's: sampled identifiers (rg-compare.repos), concept questions and member lookups
(rg-compare.questions), on every repository including the held-out and report-only ones. Sets mirror the harness's
lines: identifiers, questions, members, rust (fd identifiers, questions and members pooled), held-out questions,
held-out members, held-out rust and report-only (the repositories marked `report-only`), plus all.

monokl cost. One `monokl search <words> .` with default caps, as `rg-compare.py` runs it. Bytes are the size of its
stdout, tokens are ceil(bytes / 3) (the product's own estimate), turns are 1. The row is answerable in one turn when
one of the first 3 rows (blocks) is in the expected file, spans the expected declaration's line and shows the
declaration's text, so the agent needs no follow-up read. `monokl+read` is the same cost with one more turn for a
file read of the expected block when the row is not answerable, so a miss is not counted as free.

rg-policy cost. A fixed policy standing in for an agent that only has ripgrep. Every step favors rg:

  1. Best term. For an identifier, the identifier. For a question, the word whose `rg -n` output has the fewest
     non-test lines (at least one; ties go to the longer word, then alphabetical order), which an agent could only
     know by trying every word.
  2. Turn 1: `rg -n -S -w <best term>` over the language's source files. Test files are dropped, as monokl drops
     them. The agent reads the first 200 lines, each cut to 300 bytes, with no `./` prefix; matches are sorted by path.
  3. Turn 2, only when turn 1 matched more than 50 lines: a narrower `rg -n`, read the same way. For an identifier,
     the declaration pattern of that identifier. For a question, lines holding the two best words in either order.
     A question with fewer than two words that match has no narrower pattern and skips turn 2.
  4. Last turn: a file read of the lines of the block that holds the declaration. The extent is monokl's own, from
     the first and last line of the rows of `monokl search <symbol>` with the lean cut off (`--min-score 0`, no row
     or token cap, `--snippet-lines 0`); the declaration line is found by rg, and ranking plays no part, so the
     measurement does not depend on where monokl ranks the answer. For each declaration line the block is the
     innermost block holding it (a class does not stand in for its method), and the largest of those counts, so an
     implementation is read in place of its overload signatures. Across several expected files the smallest counts.
     A declaration with no body, such as Rust's `mod name;`, has no block and is read as its own line; the report
     lists them. The extent is monokl's, so a TypeScript block starts at the declaration and a Rust block also holds
     the doc comments and attributes above it. An analyzer extent bug would raise or lower the read cost and monokl's
     own rows alike. rg is never charged for failing to find the file: the policy always succeeds, and `rg_located`
     reports how often the expected file was in the lines the agent actually read. `scripts/test_agent_cost.py`
     checks the extents with exact bytes; `just agent-cost` runs it first.

Turns are the rg calls plus the read; bytes are the sum of the lines read in each call plus the read. `rg-early`
repeats the policy but stops, with no read, as soon as a turn shows the expected declaration's line; it is the cheaper
agent that trusts a matching line, and tokens use the same ceil(bytes / 3) as monokl.

Report only. A line starting `FAIL` is printed when a set's median monokl bytes exceed its median rg-policy bytes or
when its answerable-in-one-turn rate is below 0.8; the exit status stays 0. This is not a model evaluation: it says
what each route costs if the agent does what the policy says, not whether a model would find the answer.

Repositories are the clones `rg-compare.py` keeps in target/rg-compare, fetched on demand at the pinned shas.
"""

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Runs two monokl binaries on every cloned-repo harness question and reports output differences."""
import re
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

A, B = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
CLONES = Path("/Users/gabe/Projects/monokl/.claude/worktrees/agent-af286df18d56a59f5/target/rg-compare")
QUESTIONS = Path("/Users/gabe/Projects/monokl/.claude/worktrees/agent-aa23b683c47108dc7/scripts/rg-compare.questions")
n = same = 0
diffs = []
more_chars = trunc_block = 0
for line in QUESTIONS.read_text().splitlines():
    if line.startswith("#") or "|" not in line:
        continue
    p = [x.strip() for x in line.split("|")]
    if len(p) < 4 or not (CLONES / p[0]).is_dir():
        continue
    outs = []
    for b in (A, B):
        r = subprocess.run([b, "search", p[1], "."], cwd=CLONES / p[0], capture_output=True, text=True)
        outs.append((r.returncode, r.stdout, r.stderr))
    n += 1
    if re.search(r"\(\d+ more chars", outs[0][1]):
        more_chars += 1
    if "truncated[" in outs[1][1]:
        trunc_block += 1
    if outs[0] == outs[1]:
        same += 1
    else:
        diffs.append((p[0], p[1], outs))
print(f"runs {n}, byte-identical {same}, differ {len(diffs)}; A has '(N more chars' in {more_chars}; B has truncated[] block in {trunc_block}")
for repo, q, outs in diffs[:3]:
    a, b = outs[0][1].split("\n"), outs[1][1].split("\n")
    print("---", repo, q)
    for x, y in zip(a, b):
        if x != y:
            print("A:", x[:300])
            print("B:", y[:300])
            break
    print("B tail:", [l[:120] for l in b if not l.startswith("  ")][:6])

The `michi` name on crates.io is an unrelated project. Keep `package = "michi-core"`. | | `PartialSuccess` for timeouts | It is per-operation for batches (`completed/failed/skipped` with `index`). monokl's single search has no ops, so it does not fit. | | michi lets us choose a renderer | `OutputFormat` is `Text` (TOON) or `Json` only. low value | | Token ceiling `ceil(bytes/3)`, `max_tokens` | budget.rs:52-68, 109-123 | `truncate_by_size` (0.4) replaces the loop only partly (also offset, max_results); `BudgetSummary.max_tokens/tokens_used` (0.10.0) reports it | Loop: marginal. The adoption value is structure (machine-readable sections for a possible MCP surface), not code removal, and every added block costs tokens. ## 3. Renderer measurement (real outputs) 20 harness questions, default flags, spread evenly over the cloned repos (zustand, zod, axios, fd, fastify, trpc, date-fns), 193 rows, release binary at HEAD. Row text only (the `totalCount`/`help` tail, 2,324 bytes, is excluded from every row). Tokenizer: `o200k_base` via tiktoken; `cl100k_base` is within 1-2% in every row. Neither is Claude's tokenizer, so treat these as proxies. Rows were parsed from the TOON and re-rendered; scripts are in `/tmp/claude-501/scripts/`. | Renderer | Bytes | o200k tokens | vs TOON | In michi? | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | | TOON (current) | 34,421 | 10,177 | 0 | yes (`Text`) | | TOON without `rank`, `finalScore` columns | 32,273 | 8,744 | -14.1% | yes, a monokl column choice | | Markdown, padded (`\| a \| b \|`, `
` for newlines) | 37,562 | 12,147 | +19.4% | no | | Markdown, tight (`\|a\|b\|`) | 33,368 | 10,442 | +2.6% | no | | CSV, header once, empty for null | 32,530 | 9,608 | -5.6% | no | | TSV, header once | 32,238 | 9,666 | -5.0% | no | | Grep-style lines (`path:a-b kind [parent] sig`, snippet indented, drops rank and score) | 28,728 | 7,984 | -21.5% (lossy) | no | | JSON compact | 52,261 | 14,404 | +41.5% | `Json` | | JSON pretty | 63,861 | 20,063 | +97.1% | no | Reading: - The 8% claim does not transfer cleanly. TOON is 16% cheaper than a conventional padded Markdown table (10,177 vs 12,147), but only 2.5% cheaper than a tight one, and 5% more expensive than CSV or TSV (the `null` cells and the 2-space row indent). Against pretty JSON it is 49% cheaper, which matches the 47% claim. - Our rows are wide with free-text signature and snippet columns, so the format overhead is a small share; the cost is in the text. - The cheapest real lever is not the renderer: dropping `rank` and `finalScore` saves 14% (rank is implied by order). That is a monokl decision (and PR #113 touches the same rows); it is not a michi feature. - michi gives only TOON and JSON, so no renderer swap is available through it. A TOON-to-CSV swap would save about 5% but forfeits michi's quoting guarantees and the shared format. - Envelope blocks cost tokens, rendered by michi 0.10.0: `budget:` (4 fields) 29 tokens, `provenance:` (5 entries) 37 tokens, together about 66 tokens. The average response in this sample is 509 tokens, so both blocks on every response is about +13%. They replace no existing line. ## 4. Migration plan (at most 3 PRs) Nothing needs to wait for a michi release: 0.10.0 is out. Wait only on the demand side, in the order below. **PR A: bump to 0.10.0 and migrate (do now, small).** - Go straight to 0.10.0 (one lockstep bump); the 0.9.0 step has no migration of its own and would only add a second churn. - `Cargo.toml` pin to 0.10.0; `render_toon()` becomes `.render(OutputFormat::Text)`; `total_count` becomes a `Section::toon(..).total_count(..)`; `from_error` becomes `from_error_with_causes`; `search_row_texts` takes only the row lines. - Add a test with a signature over 200 chars that asserts the row-count/`row_texts` alignment (it fails on the unfixed bump). - Changeset: behavior-change (a `truncated[]` block in about 15% of harness queries, `...` instead of `(N more chars)`). - Trade: +0.58% tokens on the harness; one decision for the maintainer: leave the 200-char cell cut and its block, or raise `truncate_cells_at` to avoid the block at the cost of longer signatures. - Risk: textual conflict with #113 in agent.rs (rows) is possible; the findings do not depend on it. **PR B: budget and provenance (optional; I recommend not as a default).** - Adds a `budget:` and a `provenance:` block: about +66 tokens per response, with nothing deleted. That works against "fewer tokens at equal accuracy". - If wanted, emit them only on `--explain` or only when the response was truncated, and only after a structured consumer (MCP `structuredContent`) exists. The envelope types are flagged unstable by michi. - Trade: gain is machine-readable budget/provenance for a future MCP or batch surface; cost is tokens and a type that may change before michi 1.0. **PR C: diagnostics section and partial outcomes (defer).** - `PartialSuccess` and indexed ops need monokl's batch API (spec 08 section 7), which does not exist; a single search has no ops. - A `diagnostics` section would not save tokens unless grouping is kept; the timeout line has no michi equivalent. - Errors need nothing more from 0.10.0. Exit code 2 and clap usage errors stay outside michi.

The average response in this sample is 509 tokens, so both blocks on every response is about +13%. They replace no existing line. ## 4. Migration plan (at most 3 PRs) Nothing needs to wait for a michi release: 0.10.0 is out. Wait only on the demand side, in the order below. **PR A: bump to 0.10.0 and migrate (do now, small).** - Go straight to 0.10.0 (one lockstep bump); the 0.9.0 step has no migration of its own and would only add a second churn. - `Cargo.toml` pin to 0.10.0; `render_toon()` becomes `.render(OutputFormat::Text)`; `total_count` becomes a `Section::toon(..).total_count(..)`; `from_error` becomes `from_error_with_causes`; `search_row_texts` takes only the row lines. - Add a test with a signature over 200 chars that asserts the row-count/`row_texts` alignment (it fails on the unfixed bump). - Changeset: behavior-change (a `truncated[]` block in about 15% of harness queries, `...` instead of `(N more chars)`). - Trade: +0.58% tokens on the harness; one decision for the maintainer: leave the 200-char cell cut and its block, or raise `truncate_cells_at` to avoid the block at the cost of longer signatures. - Risk: textual conflict with #113 in agent.rs (rows) is possible; the findings do not depend on it. **PR B: budget and provenance (optional; I recommend not as a default).** - Adds a `budget:` and a `provenance:` block: about +66 tokens per response, with nothing deleted. That works against "fewer tokens at equal accuracy". - If wanted, emit them only on `--explain` or only when the response was truncated, and only after a structured consumer (MCP `structuredContent`) exists. The envelope types are flagged unstable by michi. - Trade: gain is machine-readable budget/provenance for a future MCP or batch surface; cost is tokens and a type that may change before michi 1.0. **PR C: diagnostics section and partial outcomes (defer).** - `PartialSuccess` and indexed ops need monokl's batch API (spec 08 section 7), which does not exist; a single search has no ops. - A `diagnostics` section would not save tokens unless grouping is kept; the timeout line has no michi equivalent. - Errors need nothing more from 0.10.0. Exit code 2 and clap usage errors stay outside michi.

` for newlines) | 37,562 | 12,147 | +19.4% | no | | Markdown, tight (`\|a\|b\|`) | 33,368 | 10,442 | +2.6% | no | | CSV, header once, empty for null | 32,530 | 9,608 | -5.6% | no | | TSV, header once | 32,238 | 9,666 | -5.0% | no | | Grep-style lines (`path:a-b kind [parent] sig`, snippet indented, drops rank and score) | 28,728 | 7,984 | -21.5% (lossy) | no | | JSON compact | 52,261 | 14,404 | +41.5% | `Json` | | JSON pretty | 63,861 | 20,063 | +97.1% | no | Reading: - The 8% claim does not transfer cleanly. TOON is 16% cheaper than a conventional padded Markdown table (10,177 vs 12,147), but only 2.5% cheaper than a tight one, and 5% more expensive than CSV or TSV (the `null` cells and the 2-space row indent). Against pretty JSON it is 49% cheaper, which matches the 47% claim. - Our rows are wide with free-text signature and snippet columns, so the format overhead is a small share; the cost is in the text. - The cheapest real lever is not the renderer: dropping `rank` and `finalScore` saves 14% (rank is implied by order). That is a monokl decision (and PR #113 touches the same rows); it is not a michi feature. - michi gives only TOON and JSON, so no renderer swap is available through it. A TOON-to-CSV swap would save about 5% but forfeits michi's quoting guarantees and the shared format. - Envelope blocks cost tokens, rendered by michi 0.10.0: `budget:` (4 fields) 29 tokens, `provenance:` (5 entries) 37 tokens, together about 66 tokens. The average response in this sample is 509 tokens, so both blocks on every response is about +13%. They replace no existing line. ## 4. Migration plan (at most 3 PRs) Nothing needs to wait for a michi release: 0.10.0 is out. Wait only on the demand side, in the order below. **PR A: bump to 0.10.0 and migrate (do now, small).** - Go straight to 0.10.0 (one lockstep bump); the 0.9.0 step has no migration of its own and would only add a second churn. - `Cargo.toml` pin to 0.10.0; `render_toon()` becomes `.render(OutputFormat::Text)`; `total_count` becomes a `Section::toon(..).total_count(..)`; `from_error` becomes `from_error_with_causes`; `search_row_texts` takes only the row lines. - Add a test with a signature over 200 chars that asserts the row-count/`row_texts` alignment (it fails on the unfixed bump). - Changeset: behavior-change (a `truncated[]` block in about 15% of harness queries, `...` instead of `(N more chars)`). - Trade: +0.58% tokens on the harness; one decision for the maintainer: leave the 200-char cell cut and its block, or raise `truncate_cells_at` to avoid the block at the cost of longer signatures. - Risk: textual conflict with #113 in agent.rs (rows) is possible; the findings do not depend on it. **PR B: budget and provenance (optional; I recommend not as a default).** - Adds a `budget:` and a `provenance:` block: about +66 tokens per response, with nothing deleted. That works against "fewer tokens at equal accuracy". - If wanted, emit them only on `--explain` or only when the response was truncated, and only after a structured consumer (MCP `structuredContent`) exists. The envelope types are flagged unstable by michi. - Trade: gain is machine-readable budget/provenance for a future MCP or batch surface; cost is tokens and a type that may change before michi 1.0. **PR C: diagnostics section and partial outcomes (defer).** - `PartialSuccess` and indexed ops need monokl's batch API (spec 08 section 7), which does not exist; a single search has no ops. - A `diagnostics` section would not save tokens unless grouping is kept; the timeout line has no michi equivalent. - Errors need nothing more from 0.10.0. Exit code 2 and clap usage errors stay outside michi.

Report and table: /Users/gabe/.claude/jobs/5bd0620b/tmp/michi-audit.md. Read-only; no commits, no PR, settings.json untouched. Experiments ran in a scratch copy (/tmp/claude-501/scratch-monokl).

**Corrections to the brief**
- michi-core 0.10.0 is published on crates.io (2026-11-16). michi #116 is the merged release PR; the envelope is michi #110-#115.
- 0.9.0 has no code change over 0.8.0. `render_toon()`, `total_count()` and `truncation()` go away in 0.10.0, not 0.9.0.
- `michi` is only a local alias. The `michi` name on crates.io is another project.
- `PartialSuccess` is per-op batch only, so it does not fit a single search.
- michi offers only TOON and JSON.
- monokl already uses michi for TOON rows, `Hint`, `TruncationOutcome::hint` and `DomainError`. What is still hand-rolled is monokl's own policy, which michi says it never computes. Deletable code is about 10-15 lines. Adoption buys structure, not savings.

**Measured on 81 harness questions (real binaries)**
- Bumping to 0.9.0 breaks 3 tests: `from_error` stops copying causes. Fix: `from_error_with_causes`.
- 12 of 81 outputs change: a `truncated[N]{row,field,removed}:` block appears and `(N more chars)` becomes `…` (+0.58% tokens).
- `search_row_texts` counts that block as rows. The debug build panics at budget.rs:111 on `zustand "create store state"`; release silently continues.
- 0.10.0 migration is about 8 changed lines. Output is byte-identical to 0.9.0 and the 1130 lib tests pass. I did not run `just ci`, clippy or nextest.
- `rg-compare.py` would read a `truncated` data row as a file name.

**Tokens, 20 queries, 193 rows, o200k (a proxy, not Claude's tokenizer)**

| Format | vs TOON |
| --- | --- |
| Padded markdown | +19% |
| Tight markdown | +2.6% |
| CSV/TSV | −5% |
| JSON, pretty | +97% |
| JSON, compact | +41% |
| Dropping rank/finalScore columns | −14% |

The 8% claim does not transfer. TOON beats padded markdown by 16% and tight markdown by 2.5%. The real lever is the columns, not the renderer. `budget:` plus `provenance:` cost about 66 tokens, about +13% per response, and replace nothing.

**Plan**
- PR A, now: go straight to 0.10.0 with the 3 call sites, `from_error_with_causes`, the `.take(rows.len())` fix and a test for a signature over 200 chars. Nothing needs to wait for a michi release.
- PR B, optional: budget/provenance only behind `--explain` or on truncation. I recommend not making it default.
- PR C, defer: `PartialSuccess` and diagnostics sections need the batch API, which does not exist.
